resources.string: What OpenWatch may read and write
OpenWatch copies what your watch and scale record into Health Connect, where OpenVitals and other apps read it. Nothing leaves the phone: the app has no internet permission.

The scale\'s body composition needs your sex and height; the walking-energy estimate needs your weight. A weight or height Health Connect holds is used instead of the one typed here.

Show what the phone is playing on the watch, and play, pause, skip and change the volume from the wrist. Works while the watch stays connected.
Notification access is off. Android only shows the phone\'s players to an app that has it. Grant it in system settings.
OpenWatch will read what your phone is playing

To show music controls on your watch, OpenWatch reads the phone's media players: the app that is playing, the track, artist and album, and how far into the track it is.

Android shows players only to an app with notification access, so the next screen asks for that. While notification forwarding is off, OpenWatch does not keep or forward your notifications.

Track details are read on this device and sent only to the watch you paired, over Bluetooth. They are never stored.

You can switch this off at any time.
Show the phone\'s upcoming events in the watch\'s calendar glance. Events go to the watch over Bluetooth and nowhere else.
Calendar access was declined. Grant it in system settings to sync events.
Whenever CoMaps is navigating, show the next turn, the distance to it and the street on the watch as a notification that updates in place. No recording needed; it works during one too.
CoMaps access was declined, so there is nothing to send. Grant it in system settings, or install CoMaps.
Import a satellite prediction file so the watch finds GPS in seconds. Nothing is downloaded: fetch the file yourself and OpenWatch hands it over when the watch asks.
That file is not GPS ephemeris data.
That file is too old to help. Ephemeris predicts where the satellites will be, so anything past a week is worse than none.
That file could not be read.

Streams heart rate and steps from the watch while it is connected, for the dashboard. Uses more watch battery.

Syncs the watch on its own, so sleep and activity arrive without opening the app. The watch has to be in range, and Android decides the exact moment, so a run can be a little late. Off means the watch is only synced when you ask.
Health Connect background access is off. A sync that runs while OpenWatch is closed still saves the watch\'s data. Body energy and the history charts catch up only when you open the app.
Keeps a link to the watch whenever it is in range. The watch can then fetch weather, find this phone, and hand over new recordings the moment they finish — at some cost to watch and phone battery.
Asks the watch for larger Bluetooth packets, which makes a sync much faster. Turn it off if the watch keeps dropping the link or a sync never gets going.
Your watch is looking for this phone
Android asks for these separately from Health Connect. Without them a watch cannot be found, and background syncs stop quietly.
Find and connect watches, heart rate straps and other sensors.
Sync progress, reminders and workout alerts.
Required to scan for Bluetooth devices on older Android versions.
Lets background syncs finish instead of being paused by battery saving. Opens Android settings.
Send phone notifications to a connected watch. Opens Android settings.

OpenWatch pairs a Garmin or Wear OS watch and a Xiaomi scale with your phone and writes what they record to Health Connect: activities, steps, floors, calories, heart rate, sleep and weight. It reads only what a sync needs, such as your weight and height, and only with your permission.
This app does not upload your health data to a cloud service, does not include ads, and does not share data with third parties.

OpenWatch is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease or medical condition. It is not a substitute for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment from a qualified healthcare professional.
Phone notifications appear on your wrist. Read on this device and sent only to this watch.
Android asks for this on its own settings screen. OpenWatch cannot request it from here.
All apps send to the watch
Turn an app off to stop its notifications reaching the watch. Everything else keeps coming through.

To show notifications on your watch, OpenWatch reads the notifications your phone receives — including their text.

They are read on this device and sent only to the watch you paired, over Bluetooth. Nothing is saved to a file or a database, and OpenWatch has no internet permission, so notifications cannot be sent anywhere else.

You can turn this off at any time, and revoke notification access from Android settings.
Copies what your watch recorded into OpenWatch. Nothing is sent to the internet.
Pairing a watch lets OpenWatch copy what it recorded — sleep stages, resting heart rate, stress and Body Battery — without sending anything to the internet.

The OpenWatch app on the watch records your heart rate and what a sleep estimate needs, and keeps a week of it. Sync copies the new heart rate into Health Connect and writes one estimated sleep session per night.
Walking calories not estimated: add your weight in Body profile or record one in Health Connect.
Walking calories not estimated: add your weight in Body profile, or allow OpenWatch to read your weight in Health Connect.
Steps not written: allow OpenWatch to write steps in Health Connect, then sync again.
Walking calories not written: allow OpenWatch to write active calories and read workouts in Health Connect to estimate them from the next sync on.
Heart rate variability not written: allow OpenWatch to write it in Health Connect, then sync again.
Breathing rate not written: allow OpenWatch to write it in Health Connect, then sync again.
Blood oxygen not written: allow OpenWatch to write it in Health Connect, then sync again.
Skin temperature not written: allow OpenWatch to write it in Health Connect, then sync again.
Resting heart rate not written: allow OpenWatch to read and write resting heart rate in Health Connect to estimate it from the next sync on.
Add a scale, and every weigh-in lands in Health Connect.
Step on the scale so it lights up, then tap Find. Android lists the scales it hears and asks whether OpenWatch may use the one you pick.
OpenWatch needs this to hear the scale.
Not known yet. Step on the scale once.
Android is not waking OpenWatch for this scale, so weigh-ins are heard only while the app is open.
OpenWatch saves each weigh-in from a Bluetooth scale as it happens, with the app open or closed. It never connects to the scale, and nothing is sent to the internet.
The scale encrypts what it sends. Pair it once in Xiaomi Home, read its Bluetooth key from your Xiaomi account with a token extractor tool, and paste the key here. It stays on this phone.
A key is 32 characters: digits and the letters a to f.
This key does not open what the scale sends. A scale paired again in Xiaomi Home gets a new key.
Weigh-ins are saved while OpenWatch is open.
